text: Every field is an integral domain.
explanation: True. A field is a commutative ring with 1 ≠ 0 in which every nonzero element is a unit; if ab = 0 with a ≠ 0 then b = a⁻¹ab = 0, so there are no zero divisors — exactly the integral-domain condition. The converse fails: ℤ is an integral domain but not a field.
